annotation.title_clean: Conseil d'État, juge des référés, ordonnance du 18 mai 2020, n° 440442, 440445 (La Quadrature du Net et Ligue des droits de l'homme)
annotation.title_en: Council of State, interim relief judge, order of 18 May 2020, Nos. 440442, 440445 (La Quadrature du Net and Human Rights League) on police drone surveillance
named_instruments_referenced: French Data Protection Act 1978 (Loi Informatique et Libertés)
annotation.summary_en: French Council of State interim order annulling a Paris tribunal ruling and ordering the State to stop using police drones to monitor COVID-19 lockdown compliance in Paris. Drone image capture counts as processing of personal data under Directive 2016/680, so it requires a regulation adopted after CNIL opinion or technical measures that prevent identification.
key_provisions_or_claims: Drones with optical zoom can collect identifying data, so the footage is personal data even if not recorded
Drone surveillance for public-order purposes falls under the Law Enforcement Directive 2016/680 and the French Data Protection Act
Using it without a prior regulatory instrument issued after a CNIL opinion is a serious and manifestly illegal breach of privacy
The State is ordered to stop drone surveillance of lockdown rules in Paris immediately
The surveillance may resume only with a legal authorisation or technical measures that make identification impossible
